subject: Model shortlist & traffic snapshot — kickoff and mutual action plan
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Lee <sasha.lee@brightline.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Model shortlist & traffic snapshot — kickoff and mutual action plan

Hi Sasha —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Per our discussion I wanted to kick off a short thread to capture the model candidates we think are a fit and the initial traffic context we need to size the Dedicated capacity and rollout. Monica and Grace are looped for the implementation and CS handoff.

Top-level summary (short):
- Model shortlist: distilled into three tiers (Low-latency small, Balanced mid-size, High-context large) with recommended quantization tiers.
- Context needs: Brightline's recent examples indicate many requests include 2–3 documents + metadata (~3–4k tokens median), a 95th percentile around 9–10k for long-search queries.
- Token volume sample: your CSV shows 1.8M monthly active users with average 6 prompts/day — initial rough active-request estimate = ~10–15M requests/mo, token estimate ~120M–200M tokens/mo depending on output length.

Requested next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Sasha / Ken: confirm a 7-day sample window we can analyze (CSV attached would be ideal).
2) Monica: deliver a model scorecard and two rollout options (canary vs instant swap) by Friday 5/22.
3) Grace: prepare token estimate workbook with conservative and optimistic lanes.
4) Michael: schedule a 30-min kickoff next week to align SLA and canary thresholds.

I'm attaching the rough scoring template we use. Monica / Grace, feel free to update with your numbers. Sasha, if Ken or procurement wants to join the kickoff, tell me preferred times.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into a short implementation sprint.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: brightline_usage_sample.csv (CSV, 22KB)
From: Sasha Lee <sasha.lee@brightline.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ken Zhao <ken.zhao@brightline.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & traffic snapshot — kickoff and mutual action plan

Thanks Michael — attaching the 7-day export from our search logs and a sample of long-query payloads. A couple clarifications:
- The 1.8M number is MAU but only ~40% are search-heavy (we estimate 700–800k actives for the model use-case).
- Output length: most replies are short (20–50 tokens) but when we synthesize docs users often request 200–600 tokens.
- SLA: we care about median <100ms and p95 <400ms for short queries; long synth requests can tolerate up to 1.5s.

Ken from procurement will coordinate contract questions separately.

—Sasha

Attachment: brightline_7day_export.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Lee <sasha.lee@brightline.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & traffic snapshot — kickoff and mutual action plan

Hi Sasha —

Downloaded the 7-day export and ran a quick pass. High-level initial model recommendations (scorecard attached):
- Candidate A (balanced-6B quantized FP16): good throughput, 1k–4k context sweet spot; best cost/perf for mid-length synths.
- Candidate B (large-13B w/ 16k context): recommended for any lane that expects >8k context regularly; higher cost but fewer prompt truncations.
- Candidate C (fast-2B distilled): excellent p50 latency for short Q/A microflows, very cost-efficient for short-turn queries.

Context guidance based on your sample: 60% of requests fit within a 4k window if we strip repeated metadata; ~12% exceed 8k. If Brightline expects those long queries to grow, I recommend enabling a hybrid routing policy: short queries to Candidate C/A and long to Candidate B.

Preliminary token volumes from the 7-day: extrapolated 30-day active-requests = ~12M requests/mo; token mix (input+output) = 140M–210M tokens/mo depending on average synth length. The attached scorecard has per-model cost projections using Redwood Optimize profiles.

I'll produce two rollout options by EOD Friday: (1) Canary (10% traffic, 2-week ramp with automatic rollback on regen-quality drift), (2) Immediate swap with staged autoscale buckets.

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_model_scorecard.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Perfect — thanks Monica and Sasha. Quick additions to the mutual action plan and timelines:
- Friday 5/22 EOD: Monica delivers the two rollout options and per-model cost lanes (confirmed).
- Monday 5/25: 30-min kickoff at 10:00am ET to align canary metrics (p50/p95 latency, quality baseline, SLA tiers).
- By 5/28: Grace to provide token-estimate workbook with conservative/realistic/growth scenarios so procurement has numbers for model/instance budgeting.

Meeting invite sent for Monday — Sasha / Ken please accept or propose alternate. We will include a short agenda: 1) rollout approach, 2) model pinning and canary metrics, 3) autoscale and fallback policy.

Michael Grant
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Lee <sasha.lee@brightline.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 12:16:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & traffic snapshot — kickoff and mutual action plan

Hi team — attaching the token estimate workbook (three lanes: conservative / realistic / high-growth) and a short notes tab describing assumptions (avg input tokens, avg output tokens per synth, retention of history). A few assumptions to call out:
- Conservative: 10M requests/mo, avg tokens/request = 15 input + 60 output -> ~750M tokens/mo (note: this assumes synthetics are rare).
- Realistic: 12M requests/mo, avg tokens/request = 40 input + 160 output -> ~2.4B tokens/mo (mix includes document synths).
- High-growth: 18M requests/mo, avg tokens/request = 60 + 300 -> ~6.66B tokens/mo.

Please review the assumptions in the notes tab before the kickoff — these materially change instance type and dedicated pool sizing.

Attachment: token_estimate_q2.xlsx (XLSX, 310KB)

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Sasha Lee <sasha.lee@brightline.ai>

Subject: Re: Model shortlist & traffic snapshot — kickoff and mutual action plan

Thanks all — received the scorecard and workbook, appreciate the level of detail. Ken and I reviewed the lanes and realistic looks like the right starting point. We accepted the Monday 10:00am ET invite. A few asks for the kickoff:
- Can Monica include a one-slide summary of expected quality tradeoffs between Candidate A and B?
- Can Grace mark the cells in the workbook that procurement should prioritize for contract sizing?

We'll be ready to share a short list of accepted SLAs from our side at the kickoff.

—Sasha
